newsitem.title: USA: Penn National gets W. Va. gaming license.
newsitem.headline: Penn National gets W. Va. gaming license.

text.p: Penn National Gaming Inc said Tuesday it received a state license to install and operate gaming machines at the company's horse racing park in Jefferson County, W. Va.

In conjunction with the placement of gaming machines, Penn National entered into a five-year technology agreement with GTECH Holdings Corp for GTECH to finance and install a video lottery system at the racetrack.
The agreement with GTECH concludes all pending litigation between the two companies, Penn National said in a statement.

Penn National Gaming has a hearing scheduled on July 23 with the West Virginia Lottery Commission to review its request to increase to 1,000 the number of gaming machines on location at the Charles Town facility.

In a separate matter, Penn National said it has secured an option to purchase 100 acres of land in Memphis, Tenn., and is submitting an application to the Tennessee State Racing Commission for the proposed development of a harness race track and off-track wagering facility.
In Tennessee, Penn National has acquired for $130,000 a twelve month option to purchase approximately 100 acres of land off of Interstate 240 in northeastern Memphis for $2.7 million.
